predecessors.name: Kushano-Sasanian Kingdom
predecessors.text: 'when the Kushano-Sasanians lost much of their domains to the invading Kidarites' in 360-370; 'The remainder went to the Sasanian Empire proper'

successors.name: Hephthalites (White Huns)
successors.text: the northern land added in 402, the Transoxiana and Syr Darya country of the Xionites' 387-401 shape; the Kidarites page puts their capital at Samarkand and the Hephthalites page has them lose…

successors.name: Sasanian Empire
successors.text: Peroz I 'brought Tokharistan briefly under Sasanian control, issuing gold coins at Balkh' in 466

successors.name: Alchon Huns
successors.text: the Kidarite remnant 'conquered by the Alchon Huns' in the last quarter of the 5th century: the 390 shape without Bactria (Gandhara and the south), the Peroz I page's 'conquered by the Alkhans in…

ledger.x: 360: the Kushano-Sasanians lose Bactria to the Kidarites.
387: the Kidarites withdraw south and the Xionites hold the north.
390: the Kidarites hold the land between Bactria and Gandhara.
402: the Kidarites hold the northern land again.
450: the Hephthalites begin to beat the Kidarites.
466: Peroz I takes Tokharistan from the Kidarites.
467: Kidarite rule ends in Transoxiana and Bactria; the remnant holds Gandhara.

wars.name: Kidarite invasion of northwestern India
wars.outcome: The Kidarites took northern Afghanistan, then Peshawar and parts of Gandhara, and the Kushan remnants around Punjab.

wars.name: Kidarite-Sasanian wars and tribute
wars.outcome: The Sasanians 'had lost many battles to the Kidarites' by Bahram IV (388-399) and paid them tribute under Yazdegerd I, Bahram V and/or Yazdegerd II; Yazdegerd II's refusal led to the war the Kidarites declared on Peroz about 464.

wars.name: Kidarite-Gupta wars
wars.outcome: The Kidarites may have fought the Guptas under Kumaragupta I (414-c.

wars.name: Peroz I's war against the Kidarites
wars.outcome: The Kidarites declared war on Peroz about 464 after Yazdegerd II refused tribute; Peroz, allied with the Hephthalites, vanquished them in 466, held Tokharistan briefly and announced the victory at Constantinople in 467; the Kidarites withdrew to Gandhara and…

certainty.note: A steppe-descended kingdom among Kushan and Sasanian successor states: no treaty line in the pages opened; the only treaty-like item (the 358 alliance of Shapur II with the Chionites) concerns the Xionites.
